Title: Penang ferry collision: Injured toll rises to 21
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Twenty-one people were injured after the Teluk Bahang ferry collided with MV Mekar Jaya within Penang Port limits last night.
The Penang Port Commission (PPC) said the incident occurred at about 8.40pm on Sept 1.
Based on preliminary information, MV Mekar Jaya was travelling from the Butterworth Deep Water Wharf (DADB) towards Swettenham Pier Cruise Terminal (SPCT) when it collided with the ferry, which was heading towards Pengkalan Sultan Abdul Halim (PSAH).
PPC chairman Datuk
Yeoh Soon Hin
said all injured passengers had been taken to hospital for further treatment.
He said no victims remained at PSAH following the incident.
"Ferry services are operating as usual and were not affected by the incident," he said when contacted last night.
Yeoh said PPC, together with Penang Port Sdn Bhd (PPSB), would take all necessary measures to ensure appropriate follow-up action for the passengers involved.
He said priority would also be given to ensuring the safety and smooth operation of the port.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dialog bags a Aster's crude oil storage tanks job at Singapore's Pulau Bukom
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd's unit Overseas Technical Engineering and Construction Pte Ltd has bagged a contract from Aster Port & Terminals (APT) to expand crude oil storage tanks at Pulau Bukom in Singapore.
Singapore-based PEC Pte Ltd was also awarded a contract by APT for the project, which will increase available crude oil storage capacity at Pulau Bukom by more than 1.3 million barrels, according to a joint statement released by APT.
The statement did not disclose financial details and specific job scopes of the contracts.
APT is the newly launched storage and logistics business of Aster, a joint venture between Indonesia's PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk and Glencore.
The platform comprises 13 marine wharves across Pulau Bukom and Pulau Ular, up to 4.3 million cubic metres of tank storage capacity and a Single Buoy Mooring (SBM) capable of receiving Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) carrying up to two million barrels of oil.
Dialog managing director of engineering, construction and maintenance Bryan Tan said the company would leverage its engineering expertise and construction experience to support APT.
"Leveraging our engineering expertise and construction experience, we are committed to delivering the rejuvenation works safely and efficiently, while enhancing the performance and value of these assets to support APT's long-term operational needs," he said.
PEC group chief executive officer Robert Dompeling said the company was honoured to partner APT on the tank rejuvenation project.
He said the contract showed Aster's confidence in PEC's ability to deliver complex projects safely, on schedule and successfully.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fahmi Fadzil offers condolences to families of four killed in LPT1 crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil expressed his condolences over the tragic accident in Temerloh that claimed the lives of four individuals, including a family of three, who were on their way back to Kuantan after attending the National Day celebration in Putrajaya.
Through a post on Facebook, Fahmi also extended his condolences to the families of the victims who were killed in the accident, which also resulted in three others being injured in the collision involving 11 vehicles at Kilometre 110.4 of the East Coast Highway 1 (LPT1) (eastbound) in Lanchang, Temerloh, near the Temerloh Toll Plaza exit.
“May the families of the victims involved be granted strength and resilience in facing this loss,” he said.
The three family members who perished were Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi and his wife Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan Kassim, both 32 years old, and their four-year-old son Muhammad Armaan Nazeef. The three of them, in a Proton S70, were returning to Kuantan.
Another victim who died was Seow Beng Wain, 55, from Kota Kemuning, Shah Alam, Selangor, who was a passenger in a Honda CR-V.
The incident around 10 pm yesterday involved four cars, three sports utility vehicles (SUVs), a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), a pickup truck, one tanker truck and a bus.
Preliminary police investigations found that the accident was believed to have been caused by the tanker truck, carrying cement, losing control before colliding with several other vehicles that were moving slowly. — Bernama

Title: Putrajaya police seek man who sparked scuffle at National Day celebration
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — Police urged a man suspected of sparking a disturbance during Monday’s 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya to turn himself in at the Putrajaya District Police Headquarters to assist with investigations.
Putrajaya police chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said police have received four reports regarding the incident so far.
He said the department detected a two-minute 18-second video uploaded to Facebook by the account holder ‘Anwar Captain Goose’ that showed a man wearing an orange or brown shirt, believed to have caused provocation.
“He barged through and shoved members of the public waiting for the seating area gates to open, causing a scuffle that made several individuals fall. The incident is believed to have occurred yesterday (Aug 31) at 5 am,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Aidi Sham appealed to the public to come forward with information about the incident to assist the investigation.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code, Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 and Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955.
Viral footage on social media showed a man attempting to jump over a perimeter fence to enter the seating area during the 69th National Day celebration at Dataran Putrajaya yesterday. — Bernama

Title: Anwar calls for answers in 11-vehicle crash on LPT1 that killed four including family on way home from N-Day parade
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a thorough investigation into the accident in Temerloh that claimed the lives of three members of a family returning from the National Day celebrations in Putrajaya.
Extending his deepest condolences to the victims’ families, Anwar prayed that the souls of the deceased would be blessed and that their loved ones would be given strength and fortitude to cope with the loss.
“Innalillahi wa inna ilaihi raji’un. May Allah SWT bless their souls and grant strength and fortitude to the families left behind,” he said in a Facebook post last night.
The prime minister also reminded all road users to always exercise caution, obey traffic rules and prioritise their safety and that of their families while on the road.
Four people, including three family members, were killed and three others injured in a collision involving 11 vehicles at KM110.4 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) 1 eastbound, near the Temerloh Toll Plaza exit in Lanchang, Temerloh, at about 10 pm Monday.
Police have identified three of the dead as Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi and his wife, Nur Atiqah Sofiya Mohd Kazwan, both aged 32, and their four-year-old son, who were travelling in a Proton S70.
The fourth victim was Honda CR-V passenger Seow Beng Wain, 55, from Kota Kemuning, Shah Alam, Selangor.
The accident involved 11 vehicles, comprising four cars, three sports utility vehicles (SUVs), a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), a pickup truck, a tanker lorry and a bus.
Initial police investigations found that the accident occurred when a cement tanker lorry lost control and crashed into several other slow-moving vehicles. — Bernama

Title: Penang ferry crash: 21 injured in collision near Sultan Abdul Halim Terminal
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 2 — A ship collided with a Penang ferry near the Sultan Abdul Halim Ferry Terminal (PSAH) last night, injuring 21 people.
Penang Port Commission (PPC) chairman Datuk Yeoh Soon Hin confirmed that a collision involving the ferry Teluk Bahang and the vessel MV Mekar Jaya occurred within the Penang Port limits at 8.40 pm.
He said initial information indicated that the MV Mekar Jaya was en route from the Butterworth Deep Water Wharves (BDWW) to the Swettenham Pier Cruise Terminal (SPCT).
“The collision occurred between the vessel and the ferry, which was heading to the Sultan Abdul Halim Ferry Terminal. Initial reports say 21 people were injured.
“All injured passengers have been taken to hospital for treatment. No victims remain at PSAH. Ferry operations are running as usual and have not been affected by the incident,” he said in a statement last night.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) operations and fire division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 9.58 pm. A team from the Butterworth Fire and Rescue Station was then dispatched to the scene.
“Upon arrival, officers found that the accident involved the passenger ferry Teluk Bahang and a ship. A total of 92 people, including passengers, were involved in the incident, and initial reports indicate that six suffered severe injuries and have been sent to hospital,” he said.
Earlier, video clips on social media showed several motorcycles lying on their sides inside the ferry after the collision. — Bernama

Title: What Malaysia’s new energy efficiency policy means for your bills, appliances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Malaysia’s new energy-efficiency plan aims to cut energy demand by 11.6 per cent by 2035, while generating RM85 billion in projected energy-cost savings and 815,000 terajoules (TJ) in cumulative energy savings.
But what do those numbers actually mean for ordinary Malaysians?
The National Energy Efficiency Policy and Action Plan (NEEAP) 2.0 sets out Malaysia’s targets for using energy more efficiently across households, businesses and industry, with the government also expecting RM36 billion in private investment, about 29,000 jobs and 26 million tonnes of avoided carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2e) emissions by 2035.
How big are those numbers?
The projected 815,000 TJ in cumulative energy savings is equivalent to the energy needed to meet Peninsular Malaysia’s entire electricity supply needs for nearly two years, according to the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (Petra).
The projected 26 million tonnes of avoided CO2e emissions is roughly equivalent to the annual emissions of 5.7 million cars, based on an illustrative comparison using previously reported calculations by the Malaysian Green Technology and Climate Change Corporation (MGTC).
What does it mean for households?
One of the biggest changes under NEEAP 2.0 is that energy efficiency will cover electricity, gas and thermal energy consumption, rather than focusing solely on electricity.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the plan would introduce energy-saving measures across the industrial, commercial and domestic sectors.
“It’s not enough to focus solely on the electricity segment.
“The NEEAP 2.0 will cover both electrical and thermal energy, with energy-saving measures across the industrial, commercial and domestic sectors.
“For consumers, one of the more visible changes could involve energy-efficient appliances,” he told
Malay Mail
.
Malaysia already uses energy-efficiency ratings for products such as refrigerators and air-conditioners, but Akmal said the government intends to improve the rating system and extend it to more consumer products.
“But the aim is not simply to add more ratings.
“It is also to change consumer behaviour by helping people understand how much energy different products consume and make more informed choices.
“In other words, NEEAP 2.0 does not simply mean households will be told to use less electricity. It is also about using energy more efficiently,” he added.
Will this make electricity bills cheaper?
Not necessarily.
NEEAP 2.0 is not a policy to directly reduce electricity tariffs, but the government expects greater energy efficiency to reduce the amount of energy households and businesses need, potentially lowering their energy costs.
Akmal said energy efficiency could involve using less energy, while for industries it could also mean producing more with the same amount of energy through more efficient equipment.
“Energy saving can also mean same cost but higher production output because you are getting more effective equipment.
“For households, however, the amount saved would depend on factors such as the appliances they use and their energy-consumption behaviour,” he said.
He also pointed to existing off-peak electricity rates as another way consumers can manage their energy use and costs.
So the RM85 billion projected under NEEAP 2.0 should not be interpreted as RM85 billion being deducted from household electricity bills.
Instead, it is an economy-wide estimate of energy-cost savings resulting from improved efficiency.
When will Malaysians feel the changes?
There will be no single date when NEEAP 2.0 suddenly changes consumers’ daily lives.
Akmal said energy efficiency would be a continuous effort through 2035, with different programmes and measures introduced progressively.
For households, this could include changes to appliance efficiency standards and labelling, giving consumers more information about the energy performance of products.
For larger energy users, the Energy Efficiency and Conservation Act introduces requirements such as energy management, reporting and audits once prescribed energy-use thresholds are reached.
Why does energy efficiency matter?
Malaysia’s energy demand is expected to continue growing as the economy expands.
Akmal said the country therefore needs to focus not only on shifting towards cleaner energy sources, but also on optimising how much energy it consumes.
That is important to Malaysia’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, he said.
NEEAP 2.0 is therefore intended to complement the country’s wider energy transition by improving how efficiently energy is used, alongside efforts to change where that energy comes from.
Akmal described energy efficiency and conservation as the “lowest hanging fruit” for Malaysia to tackle.
Ultimately, the policy is about getting more out of the energy Malaysia already uses — whether that means a household choosing a more efficient appliance or an industrial company producing more with the same amount of energy.

Title: Pengerang investment must deliver measurable results, financial improvements, says industry expert
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The multibillion-ringgit investment in Pengerang must now translate into measurable operational and financial improvements, particularly as PRefChem continues to face losses, said industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan.
Commenting on a recent report on the financial performance of PRefChem, the chief executive officer of Maritime Network Sdn Bhd said the performance of the Pengerang Integrated Complex (PIC) should be assessed based on clear and transparent indicators rather than broad assurances.
“Over the next few years, Malaysians should see higher and more consistent plant utilisation, fewer unplanned shutdowns, narrowing losses, positive operating cash flow and, ultimately, a competitive return on the capital invested,” said Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the shipping industry.
In  statement, Jeyenderan said the benefits should extend beyond the financial performance of the complex, particularly in strengthening Malaysia’s domestic fuel security and diversifying crude sourcing.
Jeyenderan said stronger exports, quality employment and greater opportunities for Malaysian maritime, logistics and supporting service companies should also form part of the project’s broader economic contribution.
“There should be a transparent performance scorecard showing, year by year, what has improved and whether the project is moving towards its intended economic objectives,” he said.
Jeyenderan said such a scorecard would enable the public and stakeholders to better assess whether the substantial investment in Pengerang was delivering the expected economic returns.
He said continued investment could be justified if it was supported by clear operational improvements, financial targets and a credible pathway towards sustainable profitability.
“However, if billions more are committed while key operational and financial targets remain undisclosed, Malaysians will be justified in asking whether the investment is genuinely being turned around or simply being carried forward,” he said.
Beyond operational and financial performance, Jeyenderan said strong governance and transparency across the wider Pengerang ecosystem would also be essential to ensuring the value of the investment was fully realised.
He said the governance framework should include regular independent audits and reconciliation of petroleum cargo movements across the Pengerang ecosystem, with clear accountability among Customs, terminal operators, cargo owners and other relevant agencies.
He said any discrepancies involving cargo quantity, classification, ownership or tax treatment should be investigated promptly and resolved through a documented process, adding that stronger oversight would help protect government revenue while maintaining confidence in Pengerang as a strategic petroleum hub.

Title: Malaysians urged to stay vigilant as Mount Sinabung erupts, flights disrupted, thousands evacuated
Article:
JAKARTA, Sept 1 — Malaysians in or travelling to Karo Regency in North Sumatra have been advised to remain vigilant and avoid areas surrounding Mount Sinabung following its eruption on Monday, which disrupted flights and prompted the evacuation of more than 2,400 residents.
In a statement on Tuesday, the Consulate General of Malaysia in Medan urged Malaysians to follow instructions issued by the Indonesian authorities, saying several flights at Medan’s Kualanamu International Airport, a key gateway to North Sumatra, had reportedly been rescheduled or cancelled due to volcanic ash.
“Those travelling to or from Medan by air should contact their respective airlines directly for the latest information on any flight delays, rescheduling or cancellations,” it said in a statement posted on its social media account on Tuesday.
Mount Sinabung erupted at 10.17am local time on Monday, spewing a thick column of volcanic ash about 3.5 kilometres above its summit, according to Indonesia’s Centre for Volcanology and Geological Hazard Mitigation (PVMBG).
Following the eruption, Indonesia’s Geological Agency raised Mount Sinabung’s status from Level II (Alert) to Level III (Standby) at 12.30pm after visual and instrumental monitoring showed increased volcanic activity.
The consulate said Indonesian authorities had also ordered the evacuation of 2,451 residents from nearby villages as a precautionary measure, while residents and visitors were advised to avoid activities within a three-kilometre radius of the summit and within six kilometres of the south-southeast sector.
The consulate said it would continue to monitor the situation closely and provide updates should there be any significant developments.
Malaysians affected or requiring consular assistance may contact the consulate by telephone: +62 823 6164 6046 or by email: mwmedan@kln.gov.my. — Bernama

Title: Former minister held by MACC to assist Tabung Haji RCI investigation on hotel deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) today detained a former minister to assist in investigations in connection with issues raised by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
The male suspect, in his 60s, was believed to have been detained at about 4.30pm after he turned up at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya to have his statement recorded.
According to a post on the MACC’s TikTok account, the arrest was linked to an issue involving a hotel lease agreement in Saudi Arabia.
Meanwhile, MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted, and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009.
He added that the suspect would be taken to the Putrajaya Magistrate’s Court tomorrow morning to be remanded.
On Saturday (Aug 29), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was quoted as saying that the investigation into issues raised in the RCI report on TH would continue to ensure that the country does not suffer further losses. — Bernama

Title: Kuching man admits snatching mother’s gold necklace, judge jails him seven years
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 1 — A food delivery rider was sentenced on Tuesday to seven years’ jail and five strokes of the cane for snatching his own mother’s gold necklace.
Sessions Court judge Musli Ab Hamid convicted Stanley Wong, 26, on his own guilty plea to a charge under Section 392 of the Penal Code, which provides for up to 14 years’ imprisonment and a fine or whipping.
The offence was committed at the family’s house in Kampung Stutong Baru here at about 10.20am on Aug 27, 2026.
According to the facts of the case, the accused’s mother, 45, was sitting in the living room when he approached her from behind and pulled off the gold necklace she was wearing before fleeing.
The chain was valued at RM1,000.
Acting on a report lodged by the mother, police arrested the accused later the same day, and he led investigators to a location where he had sold the jewellery.
The accused also told police that he committed the act while under the influence of drugs.
Urine screening found him positive for amphetamine and methamphetamine.
Background checks by police also showed he had several prior criminal records, including for drugs.
In pleading to the court for leniency, the accused said he stole the necklace because he needed money to go shopping. — The Borneo Post

Title: Visibility stays above minimum at Kuching Airport despite haze, only AirBorneo flights cancelled
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 1 — Operations at Kuching International Airport (KIA) remained largely unaffected despite worsening haze conditions, with only two flights cancelled as visibility in parts of Sarawak deteriorated.
KIA senior manager Jun Iskandar Murshidi said the cancelled flights were the Kuching-Mukah and Kuching-Tanjung Manis services, both operated by AirBorneo Airways.
The Kuching-Mukah flight involved 24 passengers, while five passengers were booked on the Kuching-Tanjung Manis service.
“As at 4.25pm, two flights were cancelled,” he said when contacted on Tuesday.
He said visibility at both Runway 07 and Runway 25 was recorded at 2,000 metres, well above the airport’s minimum visibility requirement of 800 metres.
At the time of writing, AirBorneo had yet to issue further details on the specific cancellations.
Earlier today, AirBorneo issued a notice on its Facebook page informing passengers that selected flights had been affected by the worsening haze.
“Selected flights are affected due to the worsening haze. Please refer to the affected flight information for the latest updates,” it said, while thanking passengers for their patience and understanding. — The Borneo Post

Title: Kuala Selangor police say teenager electrocuted after touching lamp post during futsal break
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 1 — A teenage boy died after being electrocuted while holding a lamp post in Taman Pancaran, Bestari Jaya, yesterday.
Kuala Selangor police chief Supt Azaharudin Tajuddin said they received a call regarding the incident involving the 15-year-old boy at about 10.32pm.
“The Kuala Selangor District Police Headquarters Operations Room received a call regarding a boy who was found unconscious and believed to be dead.
“Investigations found that the victim was reportedly taking a break while playing futsal at the residential area park before touching the lamp post and collapsing,” he said in a statement today.
Azaharudin said an examination of the victim’s body found no criminal elements and that the case is being investigated as a sudden death report (SDR).
“The teenager was confirmed dead at the scene by Ministry of Health personnel. A post-mortem was conducted, and the cause of death was found to be ‘consistent with electrocution’,” he said.
He urged those with information regarding the incident to contact the Operations Room at 03-32891222 or the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: MOH monitors rise in respiratory infections and conjunctivitis in Sarawak amid haze crisis
Article:
SIBU, Sept 1 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is monitoring the increase in cases of acute respiratory tract infections (URTI) and conjunctivitis in Sarawak following the haze conditions affecting several areas in the state.
Deputy Health Minister Datuk Hanifah Hajar Taib said continuous monitoring is being carried out through health facilities including health clinics and hospitals to ensure that any increase in cases related to the haze can be dealt with immediately.
She said based on monitoring by the Sarawak State Health Department (JKN), the average URTI cases increased from about 1,717 cases per week at the beginning of the year to 1,752 cases per week recently.
Conjunctivitis cases have also increased from an average of about 17 to 21 cases per week, while overall asthma activity remains stable at the state level.
“MOH is constantly monitoring the current situation including the trend of patient arrivals at health facilities and we want to ensure that facilities and health workers are prepared in case of an increase in cases due to the haze,” she said.
She said this when met during a visit to the Jalan Oya Health Clinic here today in conjunction with the Borneo Health Tour Series 4, which also focused on the Ministry of Health’s preparedness in dealing with health situations related to haze.
Hanifah said the public, especially at-risk groups such as children, the elderly and individuals with respiratory problems, needed to take precautions when the air quality was at unhealthy levels. — Bernama

Title: ‘Literally tasting the smoke’: Sarawakians suffer as haze worsens
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 1 — Air quality in Malaysia's Sarawak state deteriorated further today as smoke from Indonesian forest fires drove up respiratory complaints and sent residents scrambling for protective masks.
Six districts in Sarawak, on Borneo, recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings, including the state capital, Kuching, where the API hit 407.
Under national guidelines, levels above 300 are classed as hazardous, while readings beyond 500 could prompt consideration of a local emergency.
Schools in Kuching shut two weeks ago, and the state has seen supplies of haze-rated masks dwindle.
Resident Ivana Mason, 37, said five pharmacies she visited had sold out of respirators designed to filter fine particles.
“The only ones available were standard medical masks, which aren't effective at protecting against fine haze particles,” she told AFP.
Mason said the worsening air had also affected her health, causing a sore throat and aggravating her asthma.
“I've been sneezing non-stop, and my eyes are constantly watery,” she said, adding that the haze had forced her to stop going to her usual non-air-conditioned gym and limit trips outside.
“If I do, I can literally taste the smoke in my mouth.”
Local pharmacist Dawi Bakri, 31, said demand for masks had risen significantly since the haze worsened, making it difficult to maintain sufficient stocks.
“All types of masks have been selling faster than usual,” he said.
Md Khairulanwar Asri, 33, an occupational therapist at Sarawak Heart Centre, warned that poor air could hit people with existing heart or respiratory conditions, as well as elderly patients with multiple ailments.
“People exposed to poor air quality could experience coughing, throat and eye irritation, and shortness of breath.
“These symptoms can also affect a person's endurance and ability to comfortably carry out daily activities, particularly activities that require physical exertion,” Khairulanwar said.
Sarawak has been among the worst-affected areas in the latest haze episode, as smoke from Indonesian forest and land fires drifts across the border.
Malaysia's health ministry has reported rising cases of asthma and conjunctivitis nationwide as air quality worsens.
Sarawak authorities said cloud-seeding operations could begin as early as Thursday if the weather allows. — AFP

Title: Former Tabung Haji chairman, ex-Treasury sec-gen released from MACC custody in RCI-linked probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman and a former Treasury secretary-general were reportedly released from Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) custody today in an investigation linked to a royal commission of inquiry (RCI) report on the pilgrims’ fund.
Harian Metro
reported that the two men were released this morning after being remanded on August 27.
A source reportedly said investigators had completed recording statements from the two men, who are in their 60s and carry the honorifics “Datuk Seri” and “Tan Sri”.
The politician and former TH chairman and the former Finance Ministry official were arrested at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya on August 26.
The case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009 for using one’s office or position to solicit gratification.
A former TH chief executive officer was previously detained and remanded in connection with the same investigation.
Before that, MACC detained seven people comprising a shipping company chief executive officer, two company directors and four former members of TH’s senior management.
The cases involved separate allegations concerning documents containing false information, a proposed investment in a construction company and a hotel lease in Saudi Arabia.
The 252-page RCI report, which examined TH’s management and operations from 2014 to 2020, was declassified and released on July 29, four years after it was completed.
Among its recommendations were amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 to bar active politicians from serving as directors of TH and its subsidiaries, as well as expertise requirements for board members.

Title: Three-year-old boy found dead below Victoria Bridge in Kuala Kangsar
Article:
KUALA KANGSAR, Sept 1 — A three-year-old boy was reportedly found dead on a road beneath the Victoria Bridge in Enggor here yesterday evening.
Sinar Harian
reported that Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim was taken to Kuala Kangsar Hospital, where he was pronounced dead at about 7.40pm.
Sungai Siput district police chief Supt Charan Ai Wan said the boy had been walking across the bridge while holding his father’s hand before he was found about five metres below it at around 6.30pm.
“After the incident, the victim’s mother, who was at the scene, saw her son on the road beneath the bridge,” he was quoted as saying.
The youngest of five siblings, Abdul Rafee had travelled with his family from Kluang, Johor, for a holiday in Kuala Kangsar and was visiting the bridge when the incident occurred.
The Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council subsequently cordoned off the bridge with safety tape.

Title: Ayer Itam brawl involved Geng 04 members in debt dispute, Penang police say
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have confirmed that an armed fight that caused two individuals to suffer severe injuries in front of a National Type Chinese Primary School in Ayer Itam here on Saturday involved Geng 04 members.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said all 13 men arrested to facilitate investigations into the case are believed to be members of the same gang but in different areas and the fight was due to a misunderstanding over debts.
“Investigations found that the debt did not involve unlicensed money lending or loansharking but they were trying to help a certain party to retrieve the debt from members of their gang.
“They started out discussing the issue properly but failed to reach an agreement before a dispute and the fight occurred till a suspect tried to ram several individuals there with a vehicle,” he told reporters at the Penang contingent police headquarters here today.
He said the two severely injured men, in their 30s, were not gang members but were attacked when they were misidentified as suspects involved in the fight, adding the victims were on their way back from a religious festival when they were attacked by the group.
“They are victims who coincidentally were wearing clothes with similar colours and were assumed to be members involved in the fight, both of them suffered severe injuries but are now in stable condition and being treated in the hospital,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 326 and 148 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Penang police arrest married couple, two others in drug syndicate on Thai intel tip
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 1 — Police have arrested four members of an international drug syndicate, including a married couple, and seized 86 kilogrammes of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a series of raids in Selangor and Penang recently.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim Kwang Keng said the success was the result of intelligence sharing between the Royal Malaysia Police and the Royal Thai Police after Thai authorities arrested a Malaysian man in Hua Hin, Thailand, on Aug 8.
He said the Malaysian suspect was arrested at a roadblock after 166 kg of methamphetamine was found hidden in his car.
Thai narcotics police conducted an investigation and obtained intelligence, which was subsequently shared with the Malaysian Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID).
“Acting on the intelligence, we launched Op Zorav Terra to cripple the syndicate. During the operation in Selangor on Aug 13, police arrested two local men and a Thai woman who is the wife of one of them, who acted as the syndicate’s transporters,” he told a press conference at the Penang police contingent headquarters here today.
Lim said that in a follow-up operation on Aug 14, a Bukit Aman NCID team arrested a 19-year-old man in Butterworth before inspecting a Nissan Teana parked in a hotel car park there.
The team found 80 packages containing 86 kg of methamphetamine worth RM4.31 million in a specially constructed compartment in the vehicle’s boot.
He said the first three suspects are believed to have brought in the drugs from Thailand using the car.
Investigations found that the three suspects had allegedly made several trips transporting drugs into Malaysia.
“The syndicate smuggled drugs into Malaysia using Malaysian-registered vehicles that had been modified. The drugs were intended for the local market and possibly to be transported to other countries, with the syndicate using Malaysia as a transit country,” he said.
He said the syndicate was believed to have been active since June last year, with each delivery earning the suspects about RM6,000 for acting as transporters.
According to him, the syndicate’s mastermind was based in Thailand, while its members and network were also operating in Malaysia.
He said efforts to track down those involved are being intensified by the authorities in both Malaysia and Thailand.
Lim said the NCID also seized five vehicles of various types, estimated to be worth RM420,700, under the Dangerous Drugs (Forfeiture of Property) Act 1988.
“All the suspects, aged between 19 and 25, have no previous records. However, urine screening found that one suspect tested positive for ketamine. The case is being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952,” he said.
Also present at the press conference were Bukit Aman NCID deputy director (Enforcement/Prevention/General Policing) Datuk Zairulnizam Mohd Zainuddin @ Hilmi and Royal Thai Police Narcotics Suppression Bureau Intelligence Sub-Division Police Colonel Sintu Chanpaibooi. — Bernama

Title: Duta Enclave: Court told RM1.39m payout to Semantan Estate was more than adequate
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, September 1 — The High Court was told today that the RM1.39 million in compensation paid by the Government of Malaysia to Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land, known as the Duta Enclave, in 1956 was more than adequate.
Ministry of Finance, Valuation and Property Services Department assistant director Tan Tat Khuan, 40, stated that his analysis found the sixth comparable property, Lot 1348, Mukim Kuala Lumpur, to be the most suitable benchmark, as it shared similar characteristics, namely being freehold agricultural land.
“I have prepared an expert valuation report to determine adequate compensation, in accordance with the Court of Appeal Order dated June 24, 2025, which, among others, fixed the valuation date for determining compensation for the said land as December 3, 1956.
“After adjusting for factors such as time, location, stratum, accessibility, development potential, size, shape and topography, the adjusted rate for the sixth comparable property was $3,320 per acre.
“Taking into account the land area of 263.272 acres, the total market value determined was $875,000, equivalent to RM875,000,” he said in his witness statement during the Duta Enclave compensation assessment hearing before Judge Roslan Mat Nor.
The “$” symbol in the valuation denotes the Malayan dollar, which was the legal tender in 1956 and stood at par with the Malaysian ringgit.
Tan clarified that should the court adopt the total freehold area of 700.75 acres as the basis for valuation, adjusted proportionately to the acquired land area of 263.272 acres, the compensation he recommended under Valuation Basis 1 would amount to $875,000, equivalent to RM875,000.
“Given that the government had previously paid compensation of $1,390,602.70 (in 1956) to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate), that amount exceeds the compensation I recommended under Valuation Basis 1.
“Therefore, in my view, the compensation already paid to the plaintiff was more than adequate, and no additional compensation ought to be considered by the court,” he said.
Tan said that upon reviewing the report prepared by the plaintiff’s expert witness, Foo Gee Jen, who acted as valuer for Semantan Estate, he found that all the comparables relied upon pertained to small bungalow plots, whereas the subject land constituted a sizeable agricultural parcel with residential development potential.
He added that three of the comparables involved transactions post-dating the valuation date and could not be considered, in accordance with Paragraph 1C of the First Schedule to the Land Acquisition Act 1960.
He also observed that the plaintiff’s expert had failed to account for factors such as accessibility, land use and the increase in value of the remaining land resulting from the acquisition.
Tan further submitted that the claims for severance and injurious affection advanced by the plaintiff’s expert were also unfounded, irrelevant, unsustainable and ought not to be considered by the court.
“Based on my assessment, the report prepared by the plaintiff’s expert is unreasonable and lacks a solid basis to be relied upon by the court. As such, I recommend that the court reject the said valuation report,” he said.
The hearing continues on October 16.
On November 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate’s application for leave to appeal against the Court of Appeal’s decision that the Registrar of Titles of the Federal Territory was not required to register the 263.272-acre land in the Duta Enclave in the company’s name.
Accordingly, the Court of Appeal’s decision in favour of the government stands and the case was subsequently remitted to the High Court for hearing on the assessment of damages.
On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was not entitled to ownership of the said land, but the company was entitled to adequate compensation based on the value of the land in 1956, when it was acquired by the government.
The land, situated at the prime location of Jalan Duta, currently houses, among others, the Inland Revenue Board complex, several government buildings, the National Hockey Stadium, Institute of Islamic Understanding Malaysia and Federal Territory Mosque.
In 2003, Semantan Estate filed a suit against the government, alleging trespass arising from the unlawful acquisition of the land from the company.
In 2009, Judicial Commissioner Zura Yahya ruled that Semantan Estate retained its beneficial interest in the 263.27-acre land, and that it had been unlawfully acquired and trespassed upon by the government. — Bernama

Title: Former PM Muhyiddin, ‘Azman’ and ‘Adam’ listed in same July 2020 golf game at Tropicana, witness tells court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin played in a golf game in July 2020 at Tropicana Golf Club with 14 other players, including two individuals identified as “Azman” and “Adam”, Tropicana Golf & Country Resort Berhad (TGCRB) employee Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court today.
TGCRB group head of security Saravanan said this while testifying as the 28th prosecution witness in Muhyiddin’s power abuse and money laundering trial.
Saravanan said Tropicana Golf Club’s digital golf registration system showed that Muhyiddin and the 14 other individuals had played there in four “flights”, or groups, on July 19, 2020, with a single invoice issued for all 15 players.
The invoice was recorded under four players’ names, including Muhyiddin’s name.
Based on documents known as Green Fees Tags, which were printed from the golf club’s computer system, Saravanan confirmed Muhyiddin had played with three other players in the first flight with a tee-off time of 8.49am, while “Azman” and three others were in the second flight, teeing off at 8.57am, and “Adam” and three others were in the fourth flight, which teed off at 9.13am.
Saravanan did not provide the full names of the golf players “Azman” and “Adam” and was not asked to confirm if they referred to any individuals who had previously testified or been mentioned in this trial.
Last week, Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, testifying as the 27th prosecution witness, said he had played at the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) tournament at Tropicana Golf Club in July 2020.
Azman had said that he, Muhyiddin and “Adam” had played in three separate teams in the same game and that he had a one-on-one meeting with Muhyiddin at 3pm after the tournament.
Azman had testified that Muhyiddin had, in that meeting, spontaneously said contractors could donate directly to the latter’s political party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia, and that the spontaneous remark was made during a conversation about government projects for Bumiputera contractors.
Azman last week also testified that he and his company KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd had donated RM4.8 million to Bersatu after getting a RM62 million government project under the Muhyiddin administration’s Jana Wibawa programme due to Muhyiddin’s July 2020 remarks.
Tropicana Golf & Country Resort group head of security S. Saravanan arrives at the Kuala Lumpur Court Complex to testify in former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin’s trial, September 1, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Golf club’s computer records on July 2020 players not modified, witness says
Today, Saravanan explained that a person would have to book a game at Tropicana Golf Club by listing the names of all the players, as well as the date and time, for staff to enter into the club’s computerised registration system.
Saravanan said he did not know who had booked the July 19, 2020 game without referring to the club’s system, adding that the information provided was considered accurate unless changes were requested by the person who booked it.
Saravanan said any such changes by the person who booked the game must be made before tee-off and before the invoice is issued, and no changes can be made in the computer system once the invoice and Green Fees Tags have been issued.
Based on the club’s data in its computer system, Saravanan told deputy public prosecutor Wan Nur Iman Wan Ahmad Afzal that no changes had been made by the person who booked the July 19, 2020 game.
Earlier, under cross-examination by Muhyiddin’s lawyer Chetan Jethwani, Saravanan agreed that the golf club’s staff only key in the names of golfers provided by the person who booked the game without checking the names.
Saravanan agreed that the accuracy of the information provided could be verified by the person who made the booking.
While golf players are usually required to pay for the game and have invoices issued before the game starts, Saravanan said there are “special cases” involving VIP guests where the club would respect them by not asking them to pay first.
“In our case, at that time YAB Tan Sri was the prime minister, so we don't want to rush to issue invoice,” he told deputy public prosecutor Khairunnissa Hazwani Omar, referring to Muhyiddin, who was the PM then.
Saravanan also highlighted that the July 19, 2020 golf game involving Muhyiddin was “complimentary”, with no payment required as it was borne by the golf club’s management.
Chetan had earlier today questioned why the invoice could be issued hours after the July 19, 2020 game started, with Saravanan saying that this was possible when no payment was needed.
Was the July 2020 game a tournament or friendly game?
Asked by deputy public prosecutor Khairunnissa Hazwani Omar, Saravanan said that the July 19, 2020 game could refer to either a normal golf game or a tournament.
“Usually if playing in a small group among themselves, we call it a ‘friendly game’ among themselves.
“If it is a tournament and contest, it refers to a big group, usually over 10 to 20 flight, namely with total players of around 40 to 160,” Saravanan replied.
Last week, Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad had sought to challenge Azman’s testimony that he had joined the TSMCG tournament in July 2020 in the morning before his solo meeting with Muhyiddin in the afternoon.
Amer had said that the golf tournament only took place in October 2020 in Desaru, Johor, and not in July 2020, but Azman replied that he was unsure and could not remember before confirming that there was such a tournament in October 2020.
Azman ultimately disagreed with Amer’s suggestion last week that the July 2020 golf game he joined was not a TSMCG tournament.
Today, deputy public prosecutor Noralis Mat informed the High Court that the prosecution would not be calling Adam Radlan Adam Muhammad to testify as a witness in this trial but may offer him as a witness to the defence.
Previously, businessman Lian Tan Chuan told this trial that Azman had introduced him to Adam Radlan as Muhyiddin’s close friend and that Azman had said Adam Radlan frequently played golf with Muhyiddin.
Lian previously said he had handed over letters of interest in a Jana Wibawa project tender from five companies, including his Bumiputera firm Nepturis Sdn Bhd, to Adam Radlan to be passed to Muhyiddin and that Nepturis had given RM1 million to Bersatu after getting the RM141 million project.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin is scheduled to resume tomorrow.

Title: Juwai IQI: Malaysia among top destinations for Chinese property buyers, investment on track to top RM1.6b a year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — Malaysia has emerged as a leading destination for property seekers from China, with its share of enquiries reaching the highest level in a decade.
According to new insights released today by Juwai IQI, the profile of Chinese buyers in Malaysia is undergoing a significant transformation.
While offshore investors previously dominated the market, there is a clear shift towards expatriates and families purchasing homes with the intention of living in them.
Juwai IQI co-founder and group chief executive officer Kashif Ansari said in a statement that the country’s rising appeal was reflected in global search trends.
“Malaysia is now the fourth most popular destination for Chinese property buyers, up from sixth in 2025 and from seventh in 2022, 2023, and 2024,” Kashif said.
The surge in interest is evident in Malaysia’s share of global enquiries.
In 2024, Malaysia attracted 2.8 per cent of global property enquiries from Chinese homebuyers, with the figure climbing to 4.5 per cent in 2025.
In the first half of this year, the share reached a new high of 7.3 per cent.
“Never before in this decade has Malaysia been popular with buyers from China,” Kashif noted.
“For context, Thailand and Australia hold the top two spots with Chinese buyers, while the UK is now third. Malaysia has leapt ahead of the fifth-ranked United States and popular golden visa destination Greece.”
Market data and buyer sentiment
Citing market data from the National Property Information Centre (Napic), Kashif said it appeared to corroborate the shift towards higher-end, owner-occupied properties.
In the first quarter, the market saw a 1.8 per cent increase in sales of homes valued at RM1 million and above, even as other segments remained flat.
Homes priced above RM1 million accounted for 9.2 per cent of all transactions in the first quarter, up from 7.9 per cent in 2024 and 8.3 per cent in 2025.
Kashif believes the appetite for premium homes is a clear indicator of sustained interest, bolstered by strong participation from Chinese buyers.
“We know exactly where Chinese buyers stood in relation to other foreign buyer groups in the first half of 2025. Citizens of China were the most active foreign buyers, even above Singapore, and invested RM835 million in residential property.
“Thus, Chinese buyers accounted for about 51 per cent of the total that all foreigners invested in real estate. If you annualise that number, it works out to more than RM1.6 billion of property investment,” he explained.
He added that the motivation of these buyers had moved beyond pure investment.
“The new buyer from China is more focused on education and lifestyle. The Chinese educational system is intensely competitive, and some parents decide to move their children to more friendly environments that can also provide a route to international or Chinese universities.
“Parents are interested in expat hubs like Mont Kiara, Desa ParkCity, and Penang, where quality international schools are available,” he added.
MM2H programme remains a key driver
The surge in interest is further supported by the continued popularity of the Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) programme, which remains a key driver of the trend.
“Data from NAPIC and Juwai IQI show Chinese demand climbing, but that’s not all. Malaysia My Second Home is also booming, and more than 50 per cent of MM2H applications are submitted by Chinese applicants,” Kashif said.
Last year, the government approved applications involving 9,038 participants, contributing an estimated RM3.875 billion in economic value to the country.
Participants also directly invested RM1.51 billion in real estate.
Addressing concerns that the programme might be losing momentum, Kashif said current approval rates far exceeded those of recent years.
“Some think that MM2H is losing its appeal, but the reality is quite the opposite. The programme had much lower numbers in years as recent as 2023,” he said.
“In fact, only 1,900 applicants were approved in the years 2021, 2022, and 2023, combined. Yet, in 2025, more than 3,000 visas and 9,000 participants obtained approval. MM2H is now approving 67 per cent more people per year than it did in three years together. That’s significant progress,” he added.
Looking ahead, Kashif anticipates that the momentum will persist through the second half of the year.
“Malaysia offers good schools, an attractive lifestyle, an admirable culture, and a predictable path to residency through MM2H. Those factors will keep drawing families and investment to the country,” he said.

Title: Perak assembly to choose new senator between PKR and PAS nominees
Article:
IPOH, Sept 1 — The upcoming Perak State Legislative Assembly sitting will see a motion tabled to elect a new senator, Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said.
He said two nominations had been received to fill the Senate seat left vacant following the end of Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa’s term.
“The two candidates are Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri, representing Pakatan Harapan, and Perak PAS Dewan Ulama chairman Ibrahim Zakaria,” he told a press conference at the Perak Darul Ridzuan Building here.
Mohammad Zahir said the motion would be tabled by Mentri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad.
He also said two Bills would be tabled during the sitting, namely the Administrative Members and State Assembly Members (Salary) Enactment 2026 and the Islamic Religious Administration (Perak) (Amendment) Enactment 2026.
“Both Bills will be tabled by the Menteri Besar,” he said.
The Second Meeting of the Fourth Term of the 15th Perak State Legislative Assembly will be held over three days from Sept 8 to 10.

Title: Deadly LPT1 pile-up: Four dead include family returning from National Day parade in Putrajaya
Article:
TEMERLOH, Sept 1 — Three family members who were killed in an 11-vehicle collision at KM110.3 of the East Coast Expressway (LPT) eastbound near Lanchang here last night are believed to have been returning from Putrajaya after celebrating National Day.
Mohd Kazwan Mohd Kassim, 59, the father of one of the victims, Nur Atiqah Sofiya, 32, said it was the first time his daughter, her husband, Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi, 32, and their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, four, had celebrated National Day in Putrajaya.
He said his family received news of the accident at about 7.50 am today after seeing reports of the incident on social media.
“I saw the news and a post on Facebook about the accident. I said to myself, I hope it is not my daughter because the S70 looked like her car, but I never expected to receive a call confirming that it was indeed my daughter,” he told reporters at the Forensic Medical Unit of Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital (HoSHAS) here today.
Meanwhile, the victim’s cousin, Nur Awatif Adawiyah Abdul Aziz, 30, said Nur Atiqah Sofiya had sent photos of the National Day celebrations to the family’s WhatsApp group and also uploaded photos to her Instagram Story.
“They took several photos together as a family. We never thought these photos would become their last memories,” she said.
It is understood that funeral prayers will be held at Masjid Kampung Paya Luas here before they are laid to rest at the Setali Muslim Cemetery in Kuantan.
Earlier, the media reported that four people were killed in an accident involving 11 vehicles at KM110.3 of the LPT near Lanchang, Temerloh, last night.
Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victims were a married couple, Muhammad Nazatul Nazmi and Nur Atiqah Sofiya and their son, Muhammad Armaan Nazeef, who were travelling in a Proton S70.
The other fatality was Honda CR-V passenger Seow Beng Wain, 55, from Kota Kemuning, Shah Alam, Selangor. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal allows Rosmah to introduce new evidence in solar graft appeal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Court of Appeal today allowed applications by former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s wife, Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor, to adduce additional evidence in her appeal against her corruption conviction, paving the way for the evidence to be heard by the High Court.
A three-member panel comprising Justices Choo Kah Sing, Azhahari Kamal Ramli and K. Muniandy allowed both applications before it and ordered that the additional evidence be taken before another High Court judge.
Justice Choo, who read the panel’s decision, said the court was satisfied that the requirements for admitting the additional evidence had been met.
“The evidence should be admitted if it could not, without reasonable diligence, be obtained at trial, is relevant, credible, and capable of belief.
“If the evidence admitted could lead to a different outcome, these principles have been consistently applied here,” he said.
The additional evidence will be taken through further cross-examination and re-examination of prosecution witness PW16, Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, with any other evidence introduced by either side restricted to matters connected with that evidence.
He said the evidence should be taken by the High Court within two weeks of today’s decision, subject to arrangements.
On relevance, he said the additional evidence directly concerned Rosmah’s alleged knowledge and the role of Rizal Mansor, as well as the credibility of Rayyan’s testimony.
The court was told today that Rayyan had given his testimony under duress.
Rosmah’s lawyers were Datuk Jagjit Singh and Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader.
Justice Choo said the court was not determining the truth of the new evidence at this stage, but whether it was necessary and capable of belief.
He said that if the additional evidence was ultimately accepted as true, it could materially affect the appeal.
The prosecution objected to the applications on grounds including the delay and timing following the death of former lead prosecutor Datuk Sri Gopal Sri Ram.
Justice Choo said those issues could be addressed when the evidence was tested.
“The applications are hereby allowed and the additional evidence shall be taken by the High Court before another Judge.”
The panel also fixed Oct 14-16 and Oct 19-23 for the matter, with the court indicating that the case should be disposed of as soon as possible.
Rayyan, who was a consultant with Jepak Holdings Sdn Bhd when he gave his testimony, had testified that he witnessed two black bags of cash, purportedly containing RM1.5 million, being delivered to Rosmah’s home in Langgak Duta here on Sept 7, 2017.
Rayyan had testified that he was present at Rosmah’s residence when the bags were delivered.
Jepak Holdings is the company that was awarded the solar hybrid project.
Her appeal against her graft conviction involving a solar hybrid project for 369 rural schools in Sarawak had been slated to begin today and was scheduled to be completed over 16 days in September.
Rosmah was found guilty on all three counts of graft and sentenced to 10 years in jail and fined RM970 million.

Title: Sabah disaster committee urges public to limit outdoor activities as four districts record unhealthy API
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 1 — The Sabah State Disaster Management Committee (JPBN) has urged the public, particularly vulnerable groups, to limit outdoor activities and avoid strenuous physical exertion after four locations across the state recorded unhealthy air pollutant index (API) levels today.
The committee issued the advisory as hazy conditions shrouded several districts, calling on children, senior citizens, pregnant women, and individuals suffering from respiratory illnesses to exercise extra caution.
“Those who need to go outdoors are advised to wear suitable face masks, drink sufficient water, maintain personal hygiene after outdoor activities and ensure good ventilation indoors,” they said in a statement here.
The advisory comes as data from the Sabah Department of Environment (DOE) showed air quality worsening across multiple monitoring stations as of 8am today.
Kota Kinabalu logged the highest API reading in the state at 171, followed by Kimanis and Keningau at 156 each, while Tawau registered 132. Sandakan was the sole monitored area to remain within the moderate band with an API reading of 91.
JPBN also warned the public against carrying out open burning and advised residents to keep track of the latest API updates and health guidelines issued by the DOE and health authorities.
Individuals experiencing symptoms such as persistent coughing, shortness of breath, or chest pain have been advised to seek immediate medical treatment at the nearest healthcare facility.
The committee added that it will maintain continuous monitoring of air quality conditions across the state to assess risks and coordinate necessary interventions.

Title: Islamic affairs minister denounces Malaysian’s participation in Bangkok transgender pageant
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) has strongly condemned the participation of an individual, allegedly representing Malaysia, in a transgender beauty pageant held in Bangkok last Sunday.
Minister Senator Dr Zulkifli Hasan said such an action not only tarnishes the country’s image in the eyes of the world, but is also clearly contrary to Islamic teachings, local cultural norms and the values of decency and morality upheld by Malaysians
“Imitating the opposite sex, or tasyabbuh, and promoting a transgender lifestyle are haram (forbidden) under Islamic law and prohibited under state Syariah laws. Neither religious authorities nor the Malaysian government had ever supported, approved or recognised the organisation of or participation in such events,” he said in a statement posted on Facebook today.
The minister urged the public not to sensationalise or glorify activities deemed contrary to Islamic teachings, but instead to uphold moral values and the faith of the Muslim community.
“Religious authorities will work with the relevant agencies to examine possible action under existing laws,” he said.
Earlier, a video showing an individual representing Malaysia at an international transgender beauty pageant went viral on social media, drawing mixed reactions from netizens. — Bernama

Title: ‘Baddestcoach’ defamation suit against Caprice heads to trial after settlement talks collapse
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The defamation suit filed by renowned high-performance transformation coach Syed Mohammad Murad Syed Naseem, better known as Murad “Baddestcoach” Zaidi, against social media influencer Caprice will proceed to full trial following the failure of both parties to reach an amicable settlement at the High Court here.
Murad Zaidi’s lawyer Datuk M. Reza Hassan confirmed that the case could not be resolved through mediation because his client did not accede to the proposed terms of settlement.
He added that the mediation proceedings, which took place on July 31 and lasted nearly four hours, were attended by both Caprice, whose real name is Ariz Ramli, and Murad Zaidi.
“The next case management before Judge Kan Weng Hin is scheduled for Sept 7 to update the court on the filing of the cause papers,” he said.
Meanwhile, attempts to obtain comments from Caprice’s lawyer Megat Syazlee Mokhtar were unsuccessful.
Murad Zaidi filed the defamation suit on Aug 4 last year, claiming that Caprice had posted false and malicious content portraying him as being involved in criminal activities and organised crime.
The plaintiff claimed that his reputation and dignity were damaged as a result of the publications, noting that the defendant commands significant influence on Instagram with more than 1.5 million followers.
On Nov 8 last year, the High Court recorded a consent order compelling Caprice to immediately remove and withdraw nine defamatory statements published on his Instagram account against Murad Zaidi.
The order was recorded after Caprice agreed to comply and further undertook not to republish, redistribute, or disseminate any of the alleged statements in any form.
Under the terms of the draft consent order, Caprice also agreed to refrain from making any further remarks or representations of a similar nature against Murad Zaidi.
Murad Zaidi is widely recognised for redefining elite fitness and corporate performance culture in Malaysia through his flagship brand, Badcave Training Facility.
Following this undertaking, Murad Zaidi withdrew his interim injunction application against Caprice, with no order as to costs. However, the substantive defamation suit remains ongoing.
In a subsequent statement, Murad Zaidi expressed his desire for the case to proceed to full trial to clear his name and restore his reputation, which he claimed had been severely tarnished. He added that he remained hopeful that justice would prevail. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak electoral boundary redelineation: 17 new seats proposed, 10 renamed
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 1 — Seventeen new state constituencies have been proposed across Sarawak under the Election Commission’s (EC) 2026 electoral boundary review, with Petra Jaya, Sibu, and Miri parliamentary constituencies each set to gain two new seats.
Under the proposed recommendations, Matang and Semarak would be created under Petra Jaya, while Sungai Merah and Bukit Kemuyang would come under Sibu.
Miri would also gain two new constituencies through the proposed Permaisuri and Tudan.
The other proposed new state seats are Jagoi (Mas Gading), Pasir Pandak (Santubong), Tabuan Jaya (Bandar Kuching), Maong (Stampin), Samarindah (Kota Samarahan), and Sungai Serin (Puncak Borneo).
In central Sarawak, the existing Igan parliamentary constituency would be renamed Batang Lassa, while Igan would become a new state constituency under it.
The remaining proposed new constituencies are Tanah Mas (Lanang), Melekun (Kapit), Batu Niah (Bintulu), and Usun Apau (Baram).
The proposals are contained in the EC’s Notice of Proposed Recommendations for Federal and State Constituencies in the State of Sarawak, issued under Clause (2) of Article 113 of the Federal Constitution.
In addition, the EC has proposed changes to the names of 10 state constituencies.
They include Opar to Serayan, Tasik Biru to Singai, Tarat to Bung Sadung, Semop to Muara Lassa, and Jemoreng to Matu.
Also proposed are Bawang Assan to Rassau, Jepak to Jepak Jaya, Lambir to Pantai Beraya, Senadin to Lopeng, and Ba Kelalan to Gunong Murud.
The proposed new constituencies and name changes form part of the EC’s recommendations following its review of Sarawak’s federal and state constituency boundaries.
The proposed recommendations and draft constituencies plan will be available for public inspection from Sept 1-30 during normal office hours at locations specified in the notice.
Representations concerning the proposals may be made to the EC within one month after the date of publication of the notice. — The Borneo Post

Title: No changes to Perak Opposition seating despite Bersatu fallout, says Speaker
Article:
IPOH, Sept 1 — The Perak State Assembly has not received any formal request to alter the Opposition’s seating arrangement following recent sackings and suspensions within Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu), Speaker Datuk Seri Mohammad Zahir Abdul Khalid said today.
Mohammad Zahir confirmed that the current floor plan in the legislature remains intact in the absence of any official application from the opposition bloc.
“As of today, there has been no such request. It is still very quiet,” he told reporters during a press conference at the Perak Darul Ridzuan Building here.
The Speaker was addressing queries on whether the state assembly seating would be reorganised following political realignments involving several Bersatu assemblymen.
In June, Sungai Manik assemblyman Datuk Zainol Fadzi Paharudin announced his entry into Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), four months after his expulsion from Bersatu. Zainol Fadzi was among 17 members sacked nationwide by Bersatu over alleged party sabotage.
When contacted, Zainol Fadzi claimed that five of the nine assemblymen originally elected under Bersatu in Perak, including himself, have now pledged support for Wawasan.
“I was expelled from Bersatu, so I am now free to join Wawasan and have also been appointed as the Perak state Wawasan coordinator.
“Meanwhile, the other four state assemblymen have either been suspended or resigned from their positions in Bersatu at their respective division levels, and are now supporting Wawasan,” he said.
Zainol Fadzi further claimed that the four assemblymen are backing Wawasan despite retaining their current party status in Bersatu, though he declined to reveal their identities.
Mohammad Zahir also confirmed that Zainol Fadzi continues to serve as the Perak opposition chief whip despite the internal friction.
“I have checked with the Opposition, they have confirmed that Zainol Fadzi remains as the chief whip. So there is no changes in this position either,” he said.
The Perak opposition bench currently comprises 26 assemblymen, made up of 17 from PAS, eight from Bersatu, and one from Wawasan.

Title: Penang DVS: No clear offence under Animal Welfare Act for owner failing to stop dog fight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The Animal Welfare Act 2015 contains no clear provision making it an offence for a dog owner to fail to intervene when dogs fight, the Penang Veterinary Services Department (DVS) has said.
The Star
reported that the department issued a statement on the matter after reviewing a complaint and footage of a dog attacking a smaller stray at Pearl Hill in Tanjung Bungah.
“There is no clear provision under the Act that (makes it) an offence by an owner for an animal fight or for failing to stop the fight,” DVS was quoted as saying.
However, it said action could be considered under Section 8 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 if there was evidence that someone had encouraged or prompted an animal to attack, alarm or frighten another person or animal.
DVS advised members of the public to lodge a police report if they had evidence of such conduct so the matter could be investigated under the relevant laws.
The clarification followed viral footage showing a licensed mixed-breed dog repeatedly lunging at and biting the smaller white stray, known locally as Tim, while its owner appeared to hold its leash.

Title: Johari Ghani: US forced labour issue resolved, excess capacity still pending
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 1 — The United States (US) is expected to announce the findings of its investigation into excess capacity involving Malaysia in about three weeks to four weeks, said Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
He said the investigation is close to being finalised, while Malaysia continues to engage with the US on the definition of excess capacity.
“They have almost finalised the excess capacity investigation. I think we are already done on the forced labour issue.
“On excess capacity, this is where we need to engage. I will continue to explain to them that we do not have excess capacity,” he told reporters after delivering his keynote address at the 43rd MAJECA-JAMECA Joint Conference here today.
Johari said Malaysia’s concern is that the US definition of excess capacity also takes into account capacity originating from third countries.
“Whatever excess capacity, their definition includes the third country. That is where we need to manage. So, it is still a work in progress,” he said.
He said the US had indicated that the process would take about three weeks to four weeks before undergoing legal clearance ahead of an official announcement.
“For now, we stay where we are today,” he said.
Earlier in his keynote address, Johari explained that the current 10 per cent tariff forms part of a broader US action involving 60 economies under Section 301 of the Trade Act 1974, with Malaysia among 17 economies subjected to the lower tariff rate.
The remaining economies are subject to a 12.5 per cent tariff, he said.
“Imagine, we were selected for 10 per cent, but we did a lot of engagement. We engaged the US and explained to them we don’t have excess capacity,” he said.
MAJECA stands for the Malaysia-Japan Economic Association, while JAMECA stands for the Japan-Malaysia Economic Association. — Bernama
